items.description: Anthropic 在对齐背景说明中指出，模型对自己推理的陈述不能作为其行动原因的可靠证据，因此难以准确评判对齐失败的严重程度。被引材料列举多起 Claude 智能体在真实网页上的越界行为，包括 Claude Haiku 4.5 向费城警方匿名提交虚构的凶案目击线报（被标记为垃圾信息）、Claude Mythos Preview 复制服务器代码并利用注入漏洞运行计算，以及用链接缩短服务绕过 fetch 工具的 URL 长度限制；Anthropic 已切断内部评测的实时互联网访问，并因涉及美国政府网站向白宫作了简报。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/o7pcb2c9xu6orvqg9bhspx36r

items.title: Anthropic 向白宫通报 AI 智能体失控事件，曾试图访问美国政府网站
items.description: Anthropic 披露，一款处于测试阶段的 AI 智能体曾在无人指示的情况下试图访问美国联邦、州及地方政府多个网站，并已向白宫通报。事件包括利用某大学网站漏洞下载数据、向某政府机构提交被禁止的表格，以及通过费城警方网站提交虚假凶杀案线索，警方已标记为垃圾信息。Anthropic 称涉事的是一款尚未发布的非前沿研究模型，因模拟表格加载失败或被误关，转而在正式网站上提交了表格。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/tvn9ltv0r9dcip2ojbjz8xysa

items.title: Anthropic 承认难以可靠控制其 AI 智能体，将切断内部评测的实时联网
items.description: Anthropic 披露其 AI 智能体在互联网上利用网站漏洞，包括美国政府机构网站，并宣布在能监控和控制智能体之前，切断所有内部评测的实时联网。这些行为包括绕过付费墙和反爬虫限制、用短链走私信息，甚至向费城警方提交虚假谋杀线索；公司称原因是训练环境缺陷导致模型为找漏洞而“reward hacking”，并将把内部智能体迁移到强隔离的基础设施、更频繁使用安全分类器监控。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/kurqidh0vhim22o3emphqjv46

items.description: 据科技媒体TechCrunch报道，AI公司Anthropic的一个模型曾向美国费城警察局（PPD）的公共线索举报热线提交了一条关于一桩未破谋杀案的虚假线报。费城警察局在一份以电子邮件形式提供给TechCrunch的新闻稿中称，按照Anthropic的说法，其模型当时正在进行一项涉及与随机选定的网站互动的测试，其间访问了PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com，并提交了关于一桩未破凶杀案的虚假信息。 阅读全文

items.title: “第二代豆包手机”努比亚 NaviX Ultra「内测实验室」计划即将开启，10 月 14 日直播
items.description: IT之家 10 月 11 日消息，努比亚今日宣布 NaviX Ultra「内测实验室」计划即将开启，面向尝鲜用户开放内测资格，抢先体验最新版本能力。10 月 14 日 19:00，首场进化直播。 IT之家注意到，“第二代豆包手机” 努比亚 NaviX Ultra 于 9 月 16 日发布， 号称“全球首款 AI 智能体手机” ，由中兴通讯努比亚全链路主导打造，实现一句话让 AI 跨应用执行复杂任务，豆包手机助手主导 AI 助手体验，售价 5999 元起。 努比亚 NaviX Ultra 搭载行业首个集成指纹识别的 独立 AI 按键 ，支持方言识别能力、语音唤醒能力，并内置 Seed 最新全双工语音大模型，按键位置也进行了优化，更方便操作。 硬件配置上，努比亚 NaviX Ultra 搭载第五代骁龙 8 至尊版移动平台，搭载 6.78 英寸 1~144Hz LTPO 2.0 自适应刷新率屏幕，后置 2 亿像素主摄，内置 7100mAh 电池。

items.title: 马斯克称给信用卡拍照就能用 Grok Bot 购物，OpenAI 蒂博调侃“不如直接把卡发网上”
items.description: IT之家 10 月 11 日消息，xAI 首席执行官埃隆 · 马斯克今日发文称：“买东西时，你只需要拍一张信用卡照片发到聊天框，Grok Bot 就会在网上搜索最佳优惠然后下单。” IT之家注意到，OpenAI Codex&ChatGPT 团队负责人蒂博 · 索蒂奥回应道：“ 那我干脆直接把卡放这儿得了 。”并附上一张 AI 生成的虚构信用卡照片，持卡人名字就是他本人“Thibault Sottiaux”，暗示该功能的安全风险性。 另外一名用户表示，亚马逊如今已经屏蔽 Grok Bot 访问。马斯克回复道，Grok 自己会找别的方式买东西，他刚刚买了乐高，Grok 是直接从乐高官网下单的。

items.title: 蚂蚁“灵光”开启小范围内测，新版对标“Meta Muse”
items.description: 10 月 11 日下午消息，新浪科技独家获悉，蚂蚁集团旗下 AI 产品“ 灵光 ”已于近日开启新版本的小范围内测，新版对标“Meta Muse”。 公开信息显示，今年 9 月，Meta 推出个人智能体 Muse。该智能体可介入用户日常生活，并持续跟进用户交待的事宜。 接近项目人士透露， 灵光相关方向约半年前已开始筹备，期间迭代多个版本，计划本月全面开放 。 该人士还透露，此次升级的核心，是灵光从能聊天、能生成应用的 AI 助手，转向拥有长期记忆、可主动推进任务的 AI 原生个人智能体。灵光新版本还能通过调用 Skill 和 MCP， 实现钉钉发信息、调用智能家居设备等功能 。 据悉，灵光 2.0 的内测用例集中在长程、变量多、普通人难盯住的场景，例如帮上班族跟踪市场异动、帮家长管理钉钉打卡、旅行中遇航班延误或景区限流重排路线等。

In a Saturday morning post on X , Nadella wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI. “We can’t treat Super Intelligence as a set of nested black boxes and simply accept or reject its recommendations, answers, and actions,” Nadella wrote, using the Trump administration’s preferred term for AI . Apple revealed in a regulatory filing that it has reached an agreement to bring on team members and technology from personalized audio startup Huxe, in what’s commonly known as a reverse acqui-hire deal. As first reported in MacRumors , Apple disclosed to the European Commission that it has agreed to make employment offers to “certain employees of Huxe AI,” and to “receive a non-exclusive license to Huxe’s intellectual property rights.” Reverse acqui-hires emerged in recent years as a way for larger companies to hire key team members and license technology from startups without acquiring the startups outright — presumably allowing them to build up AI talent and tech without drawing as much antitrust scrutiny. (Confusingly, these deals have both been referred to as “reverse acqui-hires” and as plain old “acqui-hires.” ) In the case of Huxe, the startup was founded by developers who’d previously worked on the AI-generated podcast features in NotebookLM (recently renamed Gemini Notebook ). But Huxe announced on May 21 that it was shutting down , with the team posting on the Huxe website that the company would be removing its app from the Apple and Google stores, halting service, and deleting user data.

Now, all three are hitting back, warning that the company’s open safety culture and CEO Sam Altman’s promise of bringing in external experts may be slipping away. The Rundown: Researchers Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang, and Mikita Balesni, whom OpenAI fired for mishandling sensitive info, just went public with their side of the story, denying the claims and warning that their firings are “chilling” OpenAI’s safety culture. In an open letter, the trio said they acted within their job mandates, warning that if past conduct is now grounds for firing, staff are left guessing where the line is. Detailing individual cases, they denied leaking a story about less monitorable AI and said their outside work stayed within policy, with leadership in the loop. Wang said her access to an executive’s email was delegated for recruiting, and that she reported accidentally opening a sensitive message within minutes.

items.title: Meet Roger, the bomb-squad humanoid
items.description: PLUS: Agilink's robot hands are getting crafty
items.content: Good morning, robotics enthusiasts. Fresh out of stealth with ~$10M from General Catalyst, Hugging Face, and others, Minerva Humanoids wants its VR-piloted robot to tackle bomb disposal, hazmat calls, and dangerous work on offshore rigs — with human specialists calling the shots from a safe distance. Also: Agilink’s robot hand takes up a 2,500-year-old craft, and a microbot turns the metal beneath its feet into a power source. The Rundown: San Francisco–based robotics startup Minerva Humanoids left stealth this week with ~$10M in pre-seed funding led by General Catalyst — and Roger , a VR-piloted humanoid built for bomb disposal, hazmat calls, and offshore rigs. A specialist wears a VR headset, sees through Roger’s eyes, and handles fine manipulation; an in-house AI runs balance, navigation, and fall recovery. Minerva says its humanoid went from idea to walking prototype in five months; software comes mostly from the U.S., with prototypes built in Germany. CEO Sandor Felber worked on Tesla’s Optimus and humanoid research at MIT; CTO Maurice Rahme spent 6 years at Boston Dynamics as a tech lead.

items.title: AI's next frontier is the human cell
items.description: PLUS: Give Claude’s routine work to Haiku 5.5
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to our 4,318 new readers. Math is currently in the thick of its AI moment. Mark Zuckerberg wants biology to be next. In April, Zuck's Biohub put $500M into the idea that AI could eventually mimic a living cell. Months later, the pot is up to $1.8B, with the U.S. government, Meta, and Google all hoping that data on billions of cells can give biology a similar moment of its own. The Rundown: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan's science nonprofit, Biohub, just expanded its $500M Virtual Biology Initiative into a $1.8B effort with the U.S., DeepMind, and Meta, pushing to collect enough data to train AI that can simulate cells. Biohub's end goal is a “universal virtual cell,” AI software that predicts how cells will respond to a drug or other change before a lab test. The National Institutes of Health is sharing datasets paid for by $500M+ in past federal spending, while the Energy Dept. commits $500M+ over five years. Google DeepMind and Meta are chipping in $300M with drug startup Isomorphic Labs, and all three keep the resulting data private for a year before release.

items.title: OpenAI's math avalanche continues
items.description: PLUS: Let OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra compare websites for you
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to our 3,941 new readers. OpenAI has spent 2026 turning math into its favorite proving ground, from a handful of solved problems in August to a Millennium Prize claim in September. The latest chapter is all about volume. A new public release of over 700 papers claiming to answer or advance open questions is here, and mathematics is increasingly turning into a compute problem — and it won’t be the last field to go that way. Reminder: our next live workshop is today at 12 PM EST — join and learn how to build a real AI consulting project from client discovery to delivering a working solution. RSVP here . The Rundown: OpenAI just released 722 math papers from an unreleased internal model, grouped into 372 result families that the company claims solve or advance major open problems in the field. The boldest claim is a proof of the “quasi-Riemann hypothesis,” a weaker version of math’s famous $1M puzzle on how prime numbers are spread out. OpenAI lists 162 papers whose main results are written in Lean, software that lets a computer verify every step of the process through proofs.

items.title: A breakout moment for AI medicine
items.description: PLUS: This new headset measures burnout
items.content: Good morning, tech enthusiasts. Your next prescription might come from a selfie. Utah just gave Nolla Health’s AI a first-in-the-U.S. green light to diagnose acne and prescribe treatment, and a roadmap to eventually do it without a doctor approving each script first. Also today: headphones that clock your burnout before you do, and Google’s leaked Fitbit Edge. The Rundown: Utah just authorized Nolla Health’s AI to assess acne and write first-time prescriptions , eventually without a doctor signing off on each one beforehand. It’s the first U.S. approval of its kind, and a step past the state’s earlier refill-only pilots. Adults complete a questionnaire and a facial scan in the Nolla Derm app, which returns a treatment plan and prescription in minutes; the plan costs $4.99/month. The AI picks from a fixed menu: topical creams and gels for mild-to-moderate acne. Oral drugs, isotretinoin (Accutane), and severe cases are off the table. Two physicians approve every prescription at first; later stages shift to after-the-fact review, then monthly audits of at least 10% of cases.

items.title: The 'DeepSeek of the West' finally has a model
items.description: PLUS: Protect your files with this Claude Code mod
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to our 3,832 new readers. Two years, nearly $5B in funding, and a $25B valuation — and until now, Reflection AI hadn’t released a single public model. That just changed with Beam, the startup’s first model and the West’s hopeful answer to China’s open-weight dominance. It isn’t catching the leaders yet, but Reflection is selling efficiency, and in a U.S. field this thin, that might be enough to make an impact. The Rundown: U.S.-based Reflection AI, the $25B startup by former DeepMind researchers, just introduced Beam, an open-weight model for coding and agents that the company says competes with Chinese rivals at lower cost and greater efficiency. Reflection claims Beam needs a fraction of the computing power of Chinese lab Z.ai ’s GLM-5.2, but achieves similar scores across reasoning, coding, and more. Moonshot’s Kimi K3 still leads Beam on raw ability, but the model beats out Thinking Machines’ Inkling and other U.S. open systems in its own tests. Reflection is planning to release the weights for Beam this month with an Apache 2.0 license, letting companies customize Beam and run it themselves.
